katie (acct): hey team, client 'ArborPay' is seeing a flurry of 429s this morning from their dedicated pool. They report sustained token/s spikes ~2.5x above normal for ~10m. They say billing shows burst credits at 0.

maria (support): thanks @katie — do they have any recent deploys or config changes? any auth errors?

katie (acct): no deploys. auth looks fine, some requests show longer queue times then immediate 429s. customer pasted this snippet from their logs: `{"status":429,"retry_after":0.0,"detail":"admission: tokens-per-second quota exceeded"}`

autoscale-bot: ALERT: pool=dedicated-arbor-1 tps_window=60s peak=5200 target_slo=2000 burst_credits=0 autoscale_state=stable

cheng (sre): that alert matches admission controller denying traffic because burst credits depleted + no headroom. I can see the pool didn't scale up fast enough. checking metrics now — can you paste the exact timestamps and a sample request id?

katie (acct): sample request id: req_1882cdf. spike started at 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z. customer ran a replay load test which overshot production traffic.

maria (support): ok, confirmed. root cause looks like: (1) customer replayed high qps, (2) dedicated pool min_nodes set to 2 so autoscaler had >60s scale-up lag, (3) admission controller drained remaining burst credits and then started enforcing tps SLO -> 429s.

ben (infra): temporary mitigations: 1) enable short-term prewarm (set min_nodes=4) or bump reserved capacity for next hour, 2) route burst traffic to hosted fallback using the account's fallback policy, or 3) have customer reduce replay rate. I can run a quick prewarm if you want.

katie (acct): customer asked for fastest fix. please prewarm. they'll pause the replay if we can get capacity up.

ben (infra): doing prewarm now — running `infractl pool prewarm --pool=dedicated-arbor-1 --target-nodes=4 --duration=1h`

autoscale-bot: ACTION: prewarm_job started job_id=prewarm-2590001 target=4 eta_scale=00:00:35

cheng (sre): while prewarm is ramping: can we add a short-term admission override to allow limited token bursts from ArborPay until credits regen? need approval from ops lead. Otherwise we'll rely on prewarm + customer throttling.

maria (support): ops lead approved a 1-minute soft override at low priority to reduce customer impact. I applied `admission.override: {account: ArborPay, window:60s, factor:1.25, priority:low}`

autoscale-bot: INFO: override applied by maria (support) override_id=ov-2590001 expires=2026-03-15T09:20:40Z

katie (acct): customer confirms latency improving, 429s dropping. they're going to stagger replay. they also asked for recommendations to avoid this: any docs?

cheng (sre): recommend: 1) add headroom to min_nodes for planned replays, 2) enable graceful ramp via our load-shedding client or request smoothing, 3) prewarm jobs before large replays, 4) request longer burst credit horizons for dedicated contracts. I'll follow up with a short playbook.

maria (support): please also file a ticket to evaluate autoscaler sensitivity — scale-up thresholds look conservative for this pool. putting on infra backlog. ticket: INFRA-7310.

ben (infra): notes for postmortem: possible noisy-tenant interference? I don't see other tenants spiking on the same scheduler group, so likely client-driven. we'll keep monitoring.

katie (acct): summarizing for ArborPay: we prewarmed pool -> temporary admission override applied -> customer will throttle replay -> we created INFRA-7310 to tune autoscaler -> recommended best practices sent. customer happy for now. :thumbsup:

maria (support): closing thread but will follow up with cheng/ben on autoscaler tuning and adding a short playbook for customers doing replays.
